output.body: Suppose the rule for the derivative of x^3 is to bring down the exponent and keep everything else the same, so the exponent stays 3. Now look at a case you already understand: f(x) = x^2 is the area of a square with side x, and the derivative is its rate of change as x grows. You can estimate that rate at x = 3 by comparing f(3) = 9 with f(3.01) = 9.0601 (the difference quotient).
